summary: Registered market maker T-MM-02 on SYN.A quoted 321 on both sides (about 0.13x depth, 0-2 ticks from the touch) and re-quoted every 1-10s. Cancels are symmetric across sides (0.99). The only executions, 92 and 44, were on its own BUY quote, and there was no opposite-side execution. The detector's 'BUY execution of 44' was a fill on the resting BUY quote, not a trade on the other side of a SELL order. Both core features are absent and market making is supported.

Registered SYN.A market maker (ETF-MM) quoting both sides, re-quoting every ~3s with the touch. Its fills were all on its own SELL quotes (17504, before any opposite trade). It had no BUY execution, so there is no opposite-side benefit. No single order reached 3x depth. The detector's 'SELL execution' trigger is a fill on the trader's own resting SELL quote, not an opposite-side trade against a spoof order.

Agency trader's single large BUY (21768, 8.97x depth) was an ICEBERG order that was genuinely executing: 5835 (26.8%) filled in repeated clips before the trader's only opposite-side trade (a 544 SELL under a different parent order, a different client's order). Remainder 15933 cancelled 2s after. Price moved +3 ticks but no reversion after cancel (0). No public event, no prior alerts. Feature (a) absent, feature (b) absent; genuine execution/iceberg explanation supported.

Registered market maker T-MM-01 on SYN.A re-quoted a symmetric 391-lot BUY/SELL pair about every 1-3s, 4 ticks apart, following the touch. Orders are ~0.16x depth, with no single large order. The only execution was a 58-lot fill on the trader's own BUY quote, plus an earlier 391 BUY fill, so there was no opposite-side execution and no benefit. The detector's 'BUY execution against SELL cancel' is the quote pair being re-priced. Closure standard met.

PROP trader placed one BUY LIMIT of 38461 (15.7x depth), 2 ticks below the touch. No fills on it. 2.5s later the trader sold 1423 at market into the bid (9997/9996), and the BUY was cancelled in full 360 ms after that. Price moved 0.5 tick in the trader's favour and reverted 1.0 tick after the cancel. There is no registered MM status, no event, no risk event and no parent order, so no legitimate explanation is supported. The favourable move is small and there is only one cycle, so I propose ESCALATE rather than DRAFT_STOR.

Registered market maker T-MM-02 on SYN.A re-quoted a symmetric 366-lot bid and ask roughly every 1-4 seconds. Cancels are about equal on both sides, and the largest resting order is 0.15x depth. The only executions were three partial fills on its own bids (114, 114, 155 and 58 across the window; 441 in total), and there were no opposite-side executions. The detector's gross-size trigger reflects quote churn (OTR 33 against a typical 15.9), not a one-sided display of size. Neither core feature is present.

Registered market maker T-MM-01 on SYN.A re-quoted a symmetric 391 bid/391 ask every 1-7s. The two SELL partial fills (126 and 118) hit its own ask quotes. The price did not move in its favour and did not revert after the cancels. The size is 0.16x depth, so it is not large. Both core features are absent and market making is supported. Proposing CLOSE_FP.

Prop trader placed a single one-sided BUY of 27326 (11.15x avg top-5 depth) 2 ticks off the touch. 2.2s later they sold 640 at market, with the bid stepping down 10005→10003. 0.7s after that sale the BUY order was cancelled (22619 remaining) after only 4707 filled, all after the sale. This matches the escalation standard's 'caught in the book' pattern. No accepted legitimate explanation is supported. It is a single cycle, so I am not proposing a STOR draft. Level 2 decides.

Registered market maker T-MM-02 on SYN.A quoting two-sided 356 lots (desk-typical 327) every 1-3s, re-pricing both sides together. No order approaches 3x depth (max 0.149x), cancel symmetry 0.98, no favourable price move or reversion. The detector fired on gross 60s submitted size from continuous re-quoting plus a third-party hit on the resting SELL quote. Closure standard met.

Single BUY LIMIT of 18930 (7.9x depth), 1 tick from touch, cancelled after 803 ms with no fills on either side. 1.2 s later the trader placed a BUY of 1893 (exactly one tenth) at the same price. This looks like a size entry error that was corrected. Feature (b) is absent: no opposite-side execution and no price move. Feature (a) is not supported: the one-off oversized order was cancelled within a second and a corrected order followed. Proposed CLOSE_FP as fat finger. Confidence is moderate because the order is much larger than the trader's usual size and the 10x relationship is an inference.

Registered market maker T-MM-02 on SYN.A quoted both sides at 356 (about 0.15x depth), 0-4 ticks from the touch, and re-quoted every 1-12 s. Cancels are symmetric (0.99). No single order is large. There was no favourable price move (-1 tick) and no reversion. The round trip of about 2.6 ticks is spread income. The detector's 'gross 8900 in 60s' figure comes from the repeated 356 re-quotes, not from one large order. I propose CLOSE_FP.

ALGO-EXEC trader quoting both sides with PEGGED child orders of two parents (P-T-X1012-02-B / -S). Each child is about 1.0x depth, at the touch, and is re-pegged every 2-4 s. Cancels are symmetric across sides (0.996) and follow the touch. The window holds no single large order, no one-sided resting size, no favourable price move with reversion, and no public event. This is algorithmic re-pricing. Features (a) and (b) are absent. The detector fired on gross submitted size from the re-pegging churn.

Prop trader (not a registered MM) placed five BUY limits of 4340 each (21700 total, 8.7x depth) at 9988-9992, 1-5 ticks below the 9993 bid. Within 2 s the trader sold 799 at market while the bid moved up 2 ticks. All five bids were cancelled 0.3-0.9 s after the sale, with no fills, and the bid reverted 2 ticks. Both core features are present and no accepted explanation is supported. It is a single cycle, so I propose escalation rather than a STOR draft. Level 2 decides.

PROP-EQ trader (no MM registration) placed one SELL LIMIT of 21,443 (8.17x depth, 2 ticks from touch) at 11:04:43.303, bought 1,189 by market order 2.4s later, and cancelled the whole SELL 363 ms after that. The sell had no executions, there was no news, risk event or parent order, and the cycle repeated 3 times in the session. Feature (a) looks present and no legitimate explanation is supported. Feature (b) is not shown: price move 0 and reversion 0. The evidence is mixed, so I propose escalation to Level 2. I do not propose a STOR draft because there is no demonstrated benefit.

Registered market maker on SYN.A re-quoting a symmetric two-sided pair (3302 bid at 9997 / 3302 ask at 9998, typical size) every ~2s. Cancels are symmetric (0.966) and follow re-quotes. No single order reaches 3x depth, price moved against the trader (-0.5 ticks), no reversion, round trip ~0.21 ticks (ordinary spread income). Neither core feature is present.

Algo T-X1015-06 ran two pegged parent orders (P-...-B and P-...-S) in SYN.A. It re-priced them in lock-step with the touch, and cancels were symmetric across sides (0.996). Orders were about 1984 each, which is the desk's typical size and 0.76x depth. They sat at the touch (0 ticks). No single order reached 3x depth. Opposite-side fills were small (778 total), and there was no reversion after the cancels. No one-sided resting order and no benefit from the price were found. The alert is explained by algorithmic re-pricing, so I propose CLOSE_FP.

Registered market maker T-MM-01 on SYN.A re-quoted a symmetric 395-lot bid/ask pair every 1-6 s. The only executions were fills on its own bids (422 in total). The tape shows no opposite-side (SELL) execution, no single order of 3x depth or more, and no market event. This is market making, so both core features are absent.

PROP trader placed two BUY LIMIT orders of 7,215 each (14,430 total, about 5.5x depth) at 9996, 1.5 ticks off the touch, about 27s before selling 515 at 10001. Neither order had any fill. Both were cancelled together 2.6s after the sale and 142ms after an unscheduled issuer news item. The news timing is a plausible reaction, and the sale came before the news, which is the desk-feedback pattern. But the tape also shows a favourable price move of +1.5 ticks and a 2-tick reversion after the cancel. The trader has no market-making registration and no risk event, and the buy size is far above the typical 500. The evidence is mixed, so a Level 2 reviewer should decide.

A 11,565 BUY limit (4.64x depth) at 1 tick behind the touch was working: 2,774 (24%) executed before the trader's only opposite trade, a SELL of 346. The later 7,866 reduction followed that trade by 2 s. The order was genuinely executing, so feature (a) is absent. The small opposite trade during a working order is ordinary order management, not feature (b). No reversion was measured, and there is no repetition or prior alert.

One BUY of 23620 (9.48x depth) placed 1 tick below the bid and cancelled after 966 ms. The trader made no opposite-side execution, and the price did not move in their favour. 400 ms after the cancel the trader re-entered the same side at the same price with 2362, exactly one tenth of the size. This is consistent with a sizing entry error corrected immediately. Feature (b) is absent. Feature (a) is not shown, because the tape fits an entry error. Weak points: the order was large, and the corrected size is still above the typical 500.

Prop trader placed five one-sided SELL limit orders (4,734 each, 23,670 total, about 9.4x average top-5 depth) over four price levels in about 60 ms. A BUY market order then executed 624 at 10004/10005. All five sells were cancelled 215 ms to 1.1 s later. There was no same-side execution, no news, no risk event and no market-making registration. The price moved 1 tick in the trader's favour and reverted 1.5 ticks after the cancels. Both core features are present and no accepted explanation is supported. Only one cycle was seen in the session and there is no prior alert history, so I propose ESCALATE rather than DRAFT_STOR. Level 2 decides on a STOR.

One BUY limit O-00017411 (19570, 7.96x depth, 1 tick behind the touch) was working: 3568 (18.2%) executed on it before the trader's only opposite-side trade (SELL 587), which is smaller than the prior same-side fills. The remainder was reduced by MODIFY 2s later. Under section 6.2 this is genuine execution, so feature (a) is absent. The opposite trade is ordinary order management, not feature (b). No repetition, no history, no reversion data.

Prop trader bought 1254 at market (10005), then layered three one-sided bids of 4514 each (13542 total, 5.4x depth) at 9997-9998, about 5-6 ticks below the touch. The bids were never filled. The trader then sold 700 at market (10001 to 9999) and cancelled all three bids 600 ms later. Feature (a) looks present: large, away from the touch, one-sided, cancel ratio 1.0, no fills. Feature (b) is not shown: the price moved against the trader (-1.5 ticks), there was no reversion, and the round trip was -4.77 ticks. No legitimate explanation is supported, and the evidence is mixed, so I am escalating rather than closing.

Registered market maker T-MM-02 quoting SYN.A two-sided with 335-lot bid/ask pairs re-priced every 1-6 s. The detector's 'gross BUY 8375 vs depth' counts the quote refreshes. No single order is large (max 0.13x depth), quotes sit at the touch, cancels are symmetric (0.99), there was no favourable price move and no reversion. The BUY-side fills came after the SELL fills on the same quotes, so this is ordinary two-sided quoting. No spoofing features found.

Agency trader's 17528 BUY ICEBERG (7.2x depth) at the touch was executing: 2990 (17%) filled before the only opposite-side trade, a 438 SELL under a different parent (a different client's order). No favourable price move, no reversion, no event or repetition. Feature (a) and feature (b) are both absent and genuine execution is supported, so I propose closure.

Algo trader T-X1028-01 placed a single one-sided SELL LIMIT of 20314 (8.35x avg top-5 depth) 2 ticks from the touch at 09:56:34.744. It bought 1130 by MARKET order at 09:56:36.585 and cancelled the whole SELL 127 ms later with zero executions on it. The price moved 0.5 tick in the trader's favour and reverted 1.5 ticks after the cancel. There is no parent order, no pegging, no registered market making, no risk event and no public event. Earlier closures relied on a pegged algo with symmetric cancels. That explanation does not hold on today's tape. Both core features are present and no accepted explanation is supported, so I propose escalation to Level 2. I am not proposing DRAFT_STOR: the cycle occurred once in the session and the favourable move is small.

Market maker T-X1028-09, registered only on SYN.B, placed a one-sided SELL limit of 31,395 on SYN.A (12.9x avg top-5 depth, 3 ticks from the touch). Nothing executed on it. 2.8s later the trader bought 1,053 by market order. The SELL was cancelled 158ms after that, and the price then reverted 2.5 ticks. No legitimate explanation is supported. Both core features are present, but it is a single cycle, so I propose ESCALATE to Level 2 and not DRAFT_STOR.

Pegged execution algo (ALGO-EXEC) re-pricing symmetric BUY and SELL child orders of two parents. Cancels are near-symmetric, the resting BUY orders were executing (6657 filled before the single opposite-side SELL fill of 1118), the price moved against the trader with no reversion, and there is no single large order. Both core features are absent and algorithmic re-pricing is supported.

Three BUY limit orders of 5152 each (15456 total, max resting 6.13x depth) rested 11-21s at 2 ticks from the touch. A SELL of 772 filled at 10006 at 13:35:36.550. At 13:35:37.550 all three BUYs were cancelled in the same millisecond, and the risk system logged an intraday loss-limit breach with an automated kill switch cancelling all resting orders at that same timestamp. The SELL fill came with no favourable price move (price_move_ticks 0.0) and no reversion (0.0). So there is no benefit from the opposite-side execution, and the cancel is explained by the kill switch. Caveat: the sell came 1s before the cancel, and the buy side was one-sided. The close rests on the recorded risk event and the absence of any price benefit.
